clue.text: Walk at easy pace — better to avoid extremes

indicators.note: avoiding the extremes means the first and last letters of the word are dropped

parts.note: a better is one who bets, a gambler

explanation.surface: Advice to stroll gently rather than rush to either end of the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' looks like a comparative adjective, but it is a noun: someone who places bets.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to stroll in a slow, leisurely manner.

clue.text: Gold coin finally found under fruit machine

indicators.note: in a down entry, the coin's letter sits below the fruit

parts.note: the tomato is botanically a fruit

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word coin

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone finds a gold coin beneath a fruit machine in an arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit machine' (a British slot machine) reads as one item; the definition is just 'machine'.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a self-operating mechanical device, a robot-like machine.

clue.text: Dim student breaking shoulder

indicators.note: the student breaks into the word for shoulder, sitting inside it

parts.note: to shoulder a burden is to bear it
L is the learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A slow-witted student has broken a shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: Blear means blurred or dim, as of eyes or vision.

clue.text: Saucy material in books Heather's collected

indicators.note: the heather has gathered the books inside itself

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heather; the 's stands for 'has'
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Heather has amassed a stash of racy literature among her books.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant, whose Latin name is Erica.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually arousing writing or pictures, saucy material indeed.

clue.text: Widescreen mambo dancing involves a double act

indicators.note: the anagrammed letters take in the a
the letters of the two words dance into a new order

parts.note: the fifteen letters of these two words are the anagram fodder
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mambo filmed in widescreen features a comedy duo.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe and Wise were a much-loved British comedy duo of the 1960s and 70s, Eric Morecambe and Ernie Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The pair performed together as a comedy partnership, the classic example of a double act.

clue.text: Fuss after Kipling hero backs emperor

indicators.note: the fuss comes after the reversed name
the hero's name goes backwards

parts.note: Kim is the boy hero of Rudyard Kipling's novel of that name
ado is fuss, as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: A fuss follows when a Kipling hero supports an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado is the old Western title for the Emperor of Japan.

clue.text: White female leaving chips and fish

indicators.note: the female letter departs from the word for chips

parts.note: fries is the American word for chips
ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A white woman walks out on a dinner of fish and chips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'White' is a white wine, not a colour or person.
explanation.definitionFit: Riesling is a grape variety giving a well-known white wine.

clue.text: Anything but restrained in prison house

indicators.note: the excessive letters go inside the prison

parts.note: a cage confines like a prison
OTT is over the top, the opposite of restrained

explanation.surface: A prison house where life is anything but restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small country dwelling, a kind of house.

clue.text: Scot losing company in tightest financial assessment

indicators.note: what remains goes inside the word for tightest

parts.note: mean means stingy, so the tightest is the meanest

indicators.note: the word Scot loses its company abbreviation

parts.note: the word used as letters

explanation.surface: A Scot, losing a company, faces the strictest financial scrutiny.
explanation.walkthrough: It plays on the stereotype of the tight-fisted Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A means test checks someone's income and assets to decide eligibility for state benefits.

clue.text: Odd characters from East Sheen in German city

indicators.note: the first, third, fifth and so on letters are taken from the phrase

parts.note: the place name whose alternate letters, starting with the first, are read off

explanation.surface: Strange people from East Sheen, a London suburb, turn up in a German city.
explanation.walkthrough: East Sheen is a district of south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr region of western Germany.

clue.text: See 10
Take me with busty schoolteacher to party? C'est la vie!

indicators.note: letters that go out to party get wild and rearranged

parts.note: all the letters of these five words are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A cheeky invitation to a party with a buxom teacher, shrugged off with a French sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases express resigned acceptance that such is life and things happen as they will.

clue.text: Impaired crossing island with spouse?

indicators.note: the damaged word straddles the island letter, holding it inside

parts.note: marred means damaged or impaired

explanation.surface: A wry suggestion that marriage leaves one impaired.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is wed has a husband or wife, a spouse.

clue.text: Initially Androcles is trapped in big cat affair

indicators.note: these letters are caught inside the big cat

parts.note: the lion

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the name is used

parts.note: the name whose first letter is taken
taken as written

explanation.surface: Androcles, of the fable, is trapped with a lion and they form a bond.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fable, Androcles pulls a thorn from a lion's paw and the lion later spares him.
explanation.definitionFit: A liaison is a secret romantic relationship, an affair.

clue.text: See 10
Poet, unknown, in time associated with pen

indicators.note: joined next to the following word
the unknown goes inside the time

parts.note: an era is a period of time
z is a mathematical unknown
a pound is an animal pen or enclosure

explanation.surface: An anonymous poet of an earlier era wielding a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' looks like the writer's tool, apt for a poet, but it is an enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was the American modernist who wrote the Cantos.

clue.text: Obscene English used in explosive CNN edit

indicators.note: the English letter is placed among the rearranged ones
the letters are blown apart and reassembled

parts.note: the seven letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Offensive English language crept into a heated CNN broadcast edit.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent means offending against standards of decency, much like obscene.

clue.text: Derby date changed for sleeping partner?

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed around

parts.note: the nine letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The date of the Derby horse race has been moved.
explanation.walkthrough: A sleeping partner is a business investor who plays no active role; here it is a child's bedtime toy.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft toy bear that a child takes to bed is literally a partner in sleep.

clue.text: See 10
And not the river close to Skipton? It's up that way!

parts.note: nor means and not
taken as written

indicators.note: the close, or end, of the town name gives its final letter

parts.note: the town name whose final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A question about a river near Skipton, a Yorkshire town, answered with a direction.
explanation.walkthrough: Skipton is a market town in North Yorkshire; 'up' is the British way of saying north.
explanation.definitionFit: Places in the north are spoken of as being up there, so northern describes things in that direction.

clue.text: Warm up chicken for pagan

parts.note: to heat is to warm up
a hen is a chicken

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: reheat the chicken for a pagan guest.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen is someone not of a major religion, a pagan in old usage.

clue.text: Pale-looking old rocker sought by police?

parts.note: wan means pallid
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth devoted to rock and roll

explanation.surface: An ageing, pallid rock musician is hunted by the police.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits who loved rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A fugitive is wanted, as on a police poster.

clue.text: See 4
Saint surrounded by snakes and crows

indicators.note: the saint sits inside the snakes

parts.note: boas are large constricting snakes

explanation.surface: A saint encircled by snakes and black birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crows' looks like the birds, but it is the verb: to crow is to brag.
explanation.definitionFit: To crow is to brag triumphantly, so the verb forms are synonyms.

clue.text: Chaps bothering you? Try this!

definitions.meaning: looks like men or fellows, but means chapped skin
reads like advice on troublesome men, but recommends a soothing remedy

explanation.walkthrough: Chaps are cracks in the skin caused by cold or wind, not men.
explanation.definitionFit: This waxy salve is applied to the mouth to soothe and heal cracked skin.

clue.text: Tree's large span

parts.note: an arch spans a gap

explanation.surface: A tree with a wide spread of branches.
explanation.definitionFit: The larch is a deciduous conifer.

clue.text: Methodical attendant

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a hospital porter or helper

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for tidy, systematic habits and a noun for a hospital helper.

clue.text: Nonsense written about us causes stir

indicators.note: the nonsense is written around the word us, enclosing it

parts.note: rot is rubbish or nonsense
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nonsense printed about us provokes a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To roust is to rouse or stir someone out, as from bed.

clue.text: Unshaven hooligan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ..., stubbly, of a chin

explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a stubbly face and, as a noun, a violent troublemaker.

clue.text: Weakness — it leads us astray

indicators.note: the letters wander off course into a different order

parts.note: the nine letters of these three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A moral warning that a failing leads us down the wrong path.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental tiredness, a lack of energy.

clue.text: No diamonds around in robberies for pleasure-seekers

indicators.note: the reversed letters go inside the robberies

parts.note: heists are robberies

indicators.note: the letters are turned around, read backwards

parts.note: the word used as letters

explanation.surface: No diamonds are involved in these robberies by thrill-seekers.
explanation.walkthrough: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonists live for pleasure and enjoyment.

clue.text: Some Aberdeen terriers go in

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the phrase are used, a run inside it

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of Aberdeen and the start of terriers

explanation.surface: A few Scottish terriers from Aberdeen go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to come or go into a place.
